title: BY THE POWER OF YOUR ARM

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"By the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone-until your people
pass by, LORD, until the people you bought pass by. You will bring them in and
plant them on the mountain of your inheritance-the place, LORD, you made for
your dwelling, the sanctuary, LORD, your hands established."
- Ex 15:16b-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the phrase "the people you bought." Israel had just been purchased, and
they knew it. They had not negotiated their freedom or earned it. A price had
been paid.

Then comes a lovely word: "plant them." Not merely place them, or settle them.
Plant. It is what you do with something you intend to see grow, take root, and
last.

Slaves do not put down roots. For four hundred and thirty years, Israel had lived
in a land that was never theirs. God's intention was not just to move them
somewhere else, but to give them a place to be rooted.

And notice where: on the mountain of God's inheritance, near His sanctuary. The
plan was always to settle His people near Himself.

Jeremiah later uses the same image for those who trust God: "They will be like a
tree planted by the water" (Jer 17:8). Paul prays that believers would be
"rooted and established in love" (Eph 3:17).

If your life feels temporary and unsettled at the moment, hold on to this. God's
purpose for His people has always been rootedness, not perpetual wandering. The
wilderness was a passage, never the destination.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you feel planted or unsettled right now?
2. What are your roots actually going down into?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You bought me and intend to plant me. Root me deeply in
Your love rather than in shifting circumstances. Amen.
